name: LanguageTool
tagline: Grammar and style checker with browser extensions and premium suggestions

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month
pricing.notes: Official help checked 2026-07-30; monthly subscription listed at €19.90/month; annual options are much lower effective monthly cost.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 2,000 characters/text on the live comparison page; 3 AI rephrases/day.
tiers.notes: A separate onboarding page still states 10,000 characters, so the lower live comparison limit is used.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.notes: Also $49.90/quarter ($16.63/month effective) or $119.80 for 2 years ($4.99/month effective).

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Up to 20 users; Premium feature set.
tiers.notes: Annual-only official price is €56.90/user/year, converted using the ECB 2026-08-11 rate of €1 = $1.1540.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 2,000 characters/text on the live comparison page; 3 AI rephrases/day
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + quarterly + annual + 2-year for individual Premium; Team is annual-only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Team pricing is published in EUR; the USD value is an exchange-rate conversion and card/issuer fees or tax can change the final charge.

verdictSummary: Because the core engine is open source, a technical user can run the grammar checker locally or self-host the server for many use cases.
coreLoopDIY: Run LanguageTool locally/self-hosted, connect it to an editor/browser workflow, and optionally add LLM rewrites.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for hosted convenience, premium rules, and cross-device setup.

priorArt.name: LanguageTool
priorArt.desc: The product's own open-source core engine.

alternatives.name: Apple Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Proofread, rewrite, shorten, or change tone almost anywhere, assuming your Apple hardware made the guest list.

facts.install: Built into current macOS, iOS and iPadOS; enable Apple Intelligence and let the required models download
facts.engines: Apple on-device foundation models and, for harder requests, Apple Private Cloud Compute; optional ChatGPT is used for Compose
facts.dataFormat: Edits are applied to text in the host app rather than kept in a separate Writing Tools library; on-device requests stay local, Private Cloud Compute says request data is not stored, and optional ChatGPT receives the selected content
facts.gapVsPaid: It is convenient on supported Apple hardware, but it covers fewer languages and gives less rule-based grammar explanation and customization than LanguageTool.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Apple Intelligence-compatible Apple hardware, a supported language/region and several gigabytes of downloaded models

alternatives.name: Harper
alternatives.desc: A fast English grammar checker that stays on your device and mostly keeps its opinions to itself.

alternatives.name: Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Select text anywhere, hit a hotkey, and fix, rewrite, summarize, or obey a custom instruction without opening another tab.

facts.install: Use the portable Windows ZIP or macOS DMG; Linux currently runs from source
facts.engines: Gemini, native Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible cloud or local endpoint on Windows/Linux; the macOS port also supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, OpenRouter, Gemini, MLX and Ollama
facts.dataFormat: API keys and configuration stay on the device; the app does not retain writing or logs, and selected text goes only to the chosen cloud provider unless a local model is used
facts.gapVsPaid: It relies on generative models for corrections, so checks are less deterministic and its multilingual grammar rules and explanations are much thinner than LanguageTool's.
facts.setupBlocker: You must supply an API key or install a local model; macOS needs Accessibility permissions, while Linux installation and Wayland support remain rough

alternatives.name: WritingTool
alternatives.desc: A LibreOffice extension with long-document checks, style statistics, profiles, and local AI; installing Java is the cover charge.

facts.install: Install LibreOffice 24.2+, Java 17+, then add the downloaded .oxt LibreOffice extension
facts.engines: LanguageTool rules locally; optional AI rewriting through an OpenAI-compatible API, with local endpoints such as LocalAI specifically supported
facts.dataFormat: Checks, profiles and cached document-analysis data run on the local computer; document text is sent away only when a remote LanguageTool or configured AI endpoint is used
facts.gapVsPaid: Its LanguageTool-based checks are strong inside LibreOffice, but browser, email, mobile, and cross-application coverage are much weaker than LanguageTool's.
facts.setupBlocker: Java 17 and a recent LibreOffice are mandatory, and users must manually install and approve the extension

notes: A rare clean yes where prior art is the product's own open core.
prompt:
Build me a local grammar checker to replace LanguageTool Premium. Requirements:

- Do not reimplement the checker: run the open-source LanguageTool server locally
  (the Java 17 jar, skip Docker) on localhost:8081, started by a wrapper script.
- A CLI: `check file.md` prints issues with line numbers, grouped by rule category,
  and exits nonzero when errors are found so it works as a pre-commit hook.
- A tiny web page on localhost:4860 (Express, one textarea): paste text, see
  underlined issues with suggested fixes, click a suggestion to apply it.
- Optional LLM rewrite button: send a paragraph plus the LanguageTool findings to
  Claude or GPT (key in .env) and show the corrected version as a diff.
- Personal dictionary in a plain words.txt that the server loads, so my names and
  jargon stop flagging.
- A setup script that downloads the LanguageTool release zip, and optionally the
  n-gram data. Warn in the README: the n-gram files are about 8 GB but catch far
  more real errors.
- Everything runs locally and works offline except the optional LLM call. No
  accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: browser extensions and the premium-only rules. The open rule set is
  what we get.
- README: Java install, memory flags for the server, and wiring the CLI into git
  hooks.
